---
title: "From outcomes to distributions"
---

Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb{P})$ be a probability space. A random variable is a measurable function from outcomes to values. For the stipulated four-form pronoun space, a case variable can be defined by

$$
C(\omega)
\equiv
\begin{cases}
\mathrm{nom},&\omega\in\{\textit{he},\textit{they}\},\\
\mathrm{acc},&\omega\in\{\textit{him},\textit{them}\}.
\end{cases}
$$

Its value space and sigma-algebra are

$$
\mathcal X_C\equiv\{\mathrm{nom},\mathrm{acc}\},
\qquad
\mathcal G_C\equiv2^{\mathcal X_C}.
$$

The distribution of $C$ is the induced probability measure $\mathbb{P}_C:\mathcal G_C\to[0,1]$: for each $B\in\mathcal G_C$,

$$
\mathbb{P}_C(B)
\equiv\mathbb{P}(C\in B)
=\mathbb{P}\!\left(C^{-1}(B)\right).
$$

The notation remains fixed throughout this module. The symbols $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{P}_C$ denote probability measures and take events as arguments; expressions such as $\mathbb{P}(C=c)$ abbreviate the corresponding preimage events. Lowercase $p$, $q$, and $r$ denote PMFs; lowercase $f$, $g$, and $h$ denote PDFs; uppercase $F$ and $G$ denote CDFs.

## Random variables and one-variable distributions

We first explain [why random variables are needed](why-random-variables.qmd) and then give the [measurable-function definition](defining-random-variables.qmd). The next pages distinguish [discrete random variables](discrete-random-variables.qmd) from [absolutely continuous random variables](continuous-random-variables.qmd) and define their [probability mass functions](probability-mass-functions.qmd), [probability density functions](probability-density-functions.qmd), and [cumulative distribution functions](cumulative-distribution-functions.qmd).

## Expectations and moments

The [expected value](expected-values.qmd) is an integral with respect to a probability distribution when that integral exists. The notes then develop [expectations of functions](expectation-of-functions.qmd), [linearity of expectation](linearity-of-expectation.qmd), and [failure of finite expectations](when-expectations-fail.qmd). [Variance](variance-and-covariance.qmd), [standard deviation](standard-deviation.qmd), and [central moments](central-moments.qmd) summarize specified powers of centered values.

## Distribution families

The discrete families are [categorical](bernoulli-and-categorical-distributions.qmd), [Bernoulli](bernoulli-distribution.qmd), [binomial](binomial-distribution.qmd), [hypergeometric](hypergeometric-distribution.qmd), [geometric](geometric-distribution.qmd), [negative binomial](negative-binomial-distribution.qmd), and [Poisson](poisson-distribution.qmd). Their supports and probability mass functions differ because they represent different observation processes.

The continuous families are [uniform](uniform-distribution.qmd), [beta](beta-distribution.qmd), [normal](normal-distribution.qmd), [chi-squared](chi-squared-distribution.qmd), and [Student's t](student-t-distribution.qmd). Each page states the support, parameterization, and density or defining construction.

## Joint distributions

A [joint distribution](joint-probability.qmd) preserves value pairings from the same outcome. [Marginalization](marginal-distributions.qmd) sums or integrates out one coordinate. [Conditional independence](conditional-independence.qmd) states that one conditional distribution is invariant to an additional conditioning variable. [Conditional expectation](conditional-expectation.qmd), [covariance](covariance.qmd), and [correlation](correlation.qmd) summarize features of conditional or joint distributions.

The [chapter dependency graph](../learning-path.qmd) records the prerequisite relations among these definitions. Begin with [why random variables are needed](why-random-variables.qmd).
